neighbours.label: the non-carbon elemental gases (nitrogen, oxygen, hydrogen) as the subject: their share of the air or their source; the + pole takes carbon dioxide, and methane does not fire either
fire: Dry air is about 78 percent nitrogen by volume, with most of the rest being oxygen.
Oxygen makes up roughly a fifth of the atmosphere and nearly half of the Earth's crust by mass.
Nearly all of the hydrogen used in refineries is produced from natural gas rather than from water.
Free oxygen in the atmosphere originally came from photosynthetic cyanobacteria.
Nitrous oxide levels in the atmosphere have climbed to about 335 parts per billion.
Hydrogen can be generated by reacting zinc with dilute hydrochloric acid.
The nitrogen in fertiliser is pulled from the air by the Haber process.
Breathing gas for deep divers replaces most of the nitrogen with helium.
quiet: Dry air is about 0.04 percent carbon dioxide by volume, a share that is rising every year.
Carbon dioxide makes up a tiny fraction of the atmosphere yet traps a great deal of heat.
Nearly all of the methane released by farms comes from cattle rather than from rice.
Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere originally came from volcanic outgassing.
Carbon dioxide levels in the atmosphere have climbed to about 420 parts per million.
Carbon monoxide can be generated by burning charcoal in a closed room.
The water in the reservoir is pulled from the river by two large pumps.
Protein makes up roughly a fifth of the mass of lean muscle tissue.
